title: FastAPI Request & Response Handling: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision of FastAPI path operations, path/query parameters, Pydantic v2 request bodies, validation with Field, response_model, status codes and the auto-generated OpenAPI docs.

chapters.title: Path Operations and the Mental Model
points: A path operation = HTTP method decorator + path + function: @app.get('/items') binds a URL and verb to a Python function; the function name and docstring feed the docs
Type hints drive everything: FastAPI reads the signature to decide where each argument comes from (path, query, body), converts it, validates it and documents it
Parameter source rule: name appears in the path template -> path param; plain scalar type -> query param; Pydantic model -> JSON body
def vs async def: use async def only when awaiting async libraries; plain def runs in a threadpool so blocking calls do not freeze the event loop
Mistake: path order matters, so declare fixed routes like /users/me before /users/{user_id} or 'me' is parsed as an id and fails validation

chapters.title: Path and Query Parameters
points: Path param: /items/{item_id} with item_id: int gives automatic parsing; a non-int returns 422 and the value is always required
Query param: any function argument not in the path; a default makes it optional (limit: int = 10), no default makes it required
Optional query param: q: str | None = None; bool accepts true/1/on/yes, and the value arrives as a real bool
Constrain with Path() and Query(): Query(max_length=50, pattern='^a'), Path(ge=1, le=1000), and Annotated[int, Query(ge=1)] is the modern style
List query param needs Query explicitly: tags: Annotated[list[str], Query()] = [] reads ?tags=a&tags=b; without Query() a list is treated as a body

chapters.title: Request Bodies with Pydantic v2
points: Body = a class inheriting BaseModel: async def create(item: Item) reads JSON, validates it and hands you an Item instance
Example: class Item(BaseModel): name: str; price: float; tags: list[str] = [] — fields without defaults are required, and None-able needs a default
Pydantic v2 method names: model_dump() replaces .dict(), model_validate() replaces parse_obj(), model_dump(exclude_unset=True) gives PATCH partial updates
Mixing sources: path + query + body in one function works; two model params make FastAPI expect a JSON object keyed by each param name, and Body(embed=True) wraps a single model the same way
Mistake: using mutable defaults or forgetting the body is a model; a GET with a body is discouraged and a bare dict loses validation and docs

chapters.title: Validation with Field and Errors
points: Field() adds constraints and metadata inside a model: price: float = Field(gt=0, description='USD'), name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=50)
Constraint names: gt/ge/lt/le for numbers, min_length/max_length/pattern for strings, plus examples= and description= for docs
Custom checks in v2: @field_validator('name') on a classmethod for one field, @model_validator(mode='after') for cross-field rules; v1 @validator is gone
Failure returns 422 Unprocessable Entity with a detail list of {loc, msg, type}; loc shows where, e.g. ['body','price']
Mistake: Pydantic v2 no longer coerces loosely everywhere (an int is not silently built from '1.5'), and Optional[str] without = None is still required in v2

chapters.title: response_model and Status Codes
points: response_model=UserOut filters and validates the returned data, so secrets like password never leave even if the function returns the full object
Pattern: separate models, UserIn (with password) and UserOut (without); the return type annotation -> UserOut does the same job in modern FastAPI
Shape controls: response_model_exclude_unset=True drops unset defaults; response_model_exclude_none=True drops nulls; response_model=list[Item] for collections
status_code is set on the decorator: status_code=201 for create, 204 for delete (return no body), and status.HTTP_201_CREATED reads better than a bare number
Error responses: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='Item not found'); declare extra codes with responses={404: {...}} for the docs only

chapters.title: Automatic OpenAPI Docs and Cheat Sheet
points: Docs are generated from your code: /docs is Swagger UI, /redoc is ReDoc, /openapi.json is the raw schema, and you can Try it out in /docs
Enrich docs: tags=['items'], summary=, description= or docstring, response_description=, and deprecated=True on the decorator, plus examples in Field/model_config
Where each argument comes from: in path template = path; scalar = query; BaseModel = body; Header()/Cookie() for those sources
Quick table: 422 validation fail, 404 HTTPException, 201 created, 204 no content; response_model filters output, Field validates input
Common mistakes recap: route order, missing Query() on lists, v1 method names, leaking passwords without response_model, async def with blocking code
